newsitem.title: UK: BOE states case for consolidated bank supervision.
newsitem.headline: BOE states case for consolidated bank supervision.

text.p: Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies on Saturday set out the Bank's case for the concept of consolidated regulation of financial institutions in a speech to the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's financial markets conference.
He said this was more than ever needed since international financial firms are tending to centralise their controls.
Davies said that the concept of a "lead regulator" or "co-ordinating supervisor" is being widely discussed and raised several possibilities for tasks that the role could include.
First, the quantitative and qualitative assessment of international financial groups as a whole.
Second, the taking of a primary role in the management of emergencies.
Third, acting to ease the exchange of information between the different regulators of the group.
Fourth, longer term consideration of how supervisors' efforts could be better co-ordinated.
"The intention is that each host authority should be able to carry out these responsibilities more effectively by relying to some extent on the work of others," Davies said.
Davies noted that enthusiasm for the idea in the U.S. has been muted although commercial banks are already subject to consolidated supervision.

"More problematic is the position of the U.S. investment banking groups who, uniquely amongst the banking and securities industries in major countries, are not subject to ...consolidated supervision."

Davies noted that the debate on how these groups should be regulated tends to regarded as a largely internal matter, adding that their international reach should make the issue one of great interest and concern to the international financial community.
"We are optimistic that legislation will soon be enacted to address these concerns," Davies added. "It would certainly be disappointing if it is not."

In his speech, Davies also reiterated the Bank's view that supervision of the British banking industry should be kept separate and that it makes sense for it to to be carried out by the body that maintains the stability of the financial system -- the Bank of England.
Davies said the Bank favours a Holy Trinity rather than a Twin Peaks approach, the Trinity being regulators for financial services, banking and insurance.
